text: UPDATED REVIEW Talk about a location that just keeps getting better with age; in the 9 months since my first review the Lambertville OwowCow has seen a marked improvement in staff, an increase in options, and the ever-high-quality ice cream I have come to know and love is still amazing. PROS The ice cream is the reason you come to OwowCow. It is thick, rich, and flavorful. There is always a rotating blend of wonderful and creative flavors, ranging from traditional (three variants on vanilla and the classic "I Hate Chocolate" - the best chocolate ice cream you may ever taste) to unique, fruity, and floral. Even better, unlike some ice cream places I have been, they have no problem with you taking your time to decide - offering samples of as many flavors as you would like and taking the time to explain what is unique about the flavors. The serving sizes here are VERY generous. In a regular cup (my normal order) you get two giant scoops (of one or two flavors). Even for someone who loves ice cream and can eat a lot, I am always completely satisfied. They have a lot of other options besides just ice cream in a cup (although I rarely can bring myself to stray from my favorite). From shakes and floats (made with local sodas) to hand-made ice cream sandwiches (with cookies from a local baker), there is always something new to try. Also, during holidays they often have specialty cakes and pies available for order. We got their pumpkin ice cream pie over Thanksgiving - it was stunning! The staff are almost all very welcoming and friendly. When it is really busy, sometimes the staff are a little less chipper - but I would be too! It is nice to be welcomed with a smile. The location and ambiance is great. There are almost always enough seats if you want to stay and enjoy your deliciousness, the art on the walls is inviting, and it is close enough to downtown Lambertville that you can (if the weather is nice) walk downtown and enjoy the shops and then get ice cream on your way back to your car. CONS It is true that they are not the cheapest option in the world (a regular ice cream is $4.20), but they are in line with other places in the area of similar quality (and you get more bang for your buck compared to a high-end place like the Bent Spoon in Princeton). For me, the price isn't out of line, but we can't afford to come here every day either. And that's ok both for my wallet and my health. On a busy day parking can be tough, but usually workable. OVERALL OwowCow has become my favorite ice cream place in the whole region; enough so that my family and I will often make the half-hour or so drive from Princeton just for ice cream. All you really need to know is that the ice cream is fresh and delicious. Still on the fence? Come give it a try for yourself!

text: The fitness options in the Fairmount/Spring Garden area are pretty slim, so I'm really happy to have a hot yoga studio this close to my apartment! At this point, I've only attended two classes with two different instructors (Richard and Liz), but I anticipate on returning to Priya a lot more in the future. The studio itself is very open and has a lot of seating and storage space. They also have a cooler with different drinks and healthy snacks if you're feeling hungry post-yoga. Both instructors I've had class with were definitely more challenging than most yoga instructors I've experienced at other studios which I love. They do, however, provide a good range of modifications for people like me who are not as advanced in their yoga practice. There are some tolerable negatives, but they're definitely worth noting. First, there's no mirror in the studio. I could see that being a positive for some, but I like to see that my body is actually doing what it's supposed to through some of the poses. Second, the heat comes from the ceiling, and if you don't pay attention to where you place your mat, your hot yoga class will be especially hot with the heated air blasting at you. And third, both classes I've attended (7:15 pm classes) have been PACKED. Priya has tape marks to etch where mats should be placed, and there are barely a few inches between where each of the mats are on the ground. This makes it more difficult to do some of the poses that require more space, and you'll definitely end up bumping sweaty limbs with your neighbor. All-in-all, Priya's instruction seems to be above average, AND it's located so close to where I live. That's a win in my book.

text: I try my hardest to be a "wise consumer of health care." Isn't that what we're supposed to do? I called both my health insurance carrier and the provider before my daughter's appointment. My carrier confirmed the provider was in network and said to make sure the urgent care center was not physically connected to the hospital. The provider's office staff confirmed that they were not physically connected to the hospital, but they couldn't give me any details on how services would be billed. I found that odd, but my daughter needed to be seen. And given that the urgent care was quite a ways from the hospital, I thought we'd be safe. Now, seeing all the negative reviews about the same thing, I find it hard to believe the office staff didn't know how the services would be billed. When my daughter came home from her visit, I noticed she was charged a $40 copay instead of $25 and the header on the receipt said "Oro Valley Hospital." I immediately called the phone number on the receipt and was told by the CSR that they could see the visit in their system and it was coming through "right now" as an office visit, and if we were overcharged, we'd receive a refund. Turns out, they billed the charges as outpatient hospital, which under many plans, including mine, is subject to deductible. Long story short, this little visit cost $285 after insurance even though I tried to do everything right. We won't come back unless it's an emergency and in that case, we'll go to the emergency room at the hospital.

Why would I say this? 1, It's sauces are so fresh, fragrant, flavorful and it really brings the meals home! The Verde/Green Sauce is a hit for those that prefer heat. The Red Sauce is great for anyone. 2, When you meet Antonio the owner/cook and talk to him about his food, you can tell he wouldn't compromise on ingredients, he takes a lot of pride in his traditional meals and gets excited when others enjoy it. Like any good chef, when we gave him our compliments, he was ear to ear smiles. 3, We leaned over the ordering counter and asked him what the gigantic pot (so big it took up most of the stove) was. He said, I'm already starting the food for tomorrow. Seeing the beautiful food steaming and simmering over the hot stove meant only one thing. We are coming back! We were so disappointed that we had no more room in our stomachs to try the other meals. When we got the bill, my boyfriend chuckled and said this is our new spot and we can afford to eat out several nights a week here. What a gem, crazy good food, friendly owner and it was cheap! This place is only going to grow in popularity and as it does, we hope Antonio keeps his reasonable prices - it just means we'll be seeing him more often. Tips: -Come hungry and you'll be glad you did. -Pulled pork tacos are a hit so don't come late expecting there to be any left to order. Cactus is the other item that runs out. -This is very casual and rather tiny place with just a handful of tables and chairs so be ready to do an order to go. If you rather authentic than the Americanized tacos, the food leave you happy and satisfied!

text: As a huge supporter of local businesses, very seldom do I leave negative reviews; however, based on my experience at Coyote Crossing last Friday evening, I feel inclined to provide feedback. While the new decor is nice, quality of food and service have been sacrificed. As a long-time former resident of Conshohocken and self-proclaimed foodie, we have dined at Coyote Crossing 25+ times over the past 18 years. We've celebrated graduations, first dates, birthdays, engagements (you get the point) dining here. We've brought out-of-town friends and family on many occasions to have the 'meal of their life.' Last Friday, we gathered three other couples to celebrate my birthday; touting that Coyote Crossing would be a place they love. Upon arrival, we entered the 'foyer' area where a male server was loudly and profanely speaking to the older, blonde woman (who I assume manages the front of the house while the owner, Carlos saunters around the restaurant/bar area). The server was furious about a group of people wanting separate checks, post-delivery of the bill. Okay, definitely an inconvenience; but, take the drama elsewhere. We then entered the bar area and ordered over-priced watered down margaritas (Note: historically, margaritas were the establishment's wheelhouse) while waiting for the rest of our group to arrive. We were promptly seated upon their arrival and not given a hard time as they were running late... that, I definitely appreciated. Once seated, we ordered several appetizers; but, yet, the server kept pushing some sampler plate and wouldn't take "no" for an answer. I get it, the staff is probably told to push the dish; but, the sales pitch made us uncomfortable. Especially after already ordering 5+ appetizers. To sum up the rest of the dinner, we had to beg for a first round of water and then the glasses were never refilled through the entire meal. Overall, the food was HORRIBLE. The tampiquena used to be a menu "special" addition and now it's a menu standard (and $9 higher than before). The meat was either undercooked/overcooked, the enchiladas were flavorless and the accompanying rice and beans were mush. The shrimp smelled/tasted entirely too fishy and the texture was sinewy. The tortilla chips were cold and chewy and there was a hair in the pico de gallo. Even the presentation of the meal has gone from classy (there used to be a cool leaf beneath the tampiquena) to resemble that of a cafeteria. I could go on an on... The bill for seven adults (each only had 1 or 2 drinks), including tip was $450. We could have saved $300 and eaten a better meal at one of the local pubs on Fayette Street. Carlos and Coyote Crossing Management....I urge you to stick to what you know and put passionate people back in the kitchen as well as the bar. For business sake, I hope expansion of the indoor bar doesn't decrease business on the once fun, now teeny-tiny outdoor area. Good luck.

text: In the past year a lot has changed at Sabor for Christian Mena and Lino Oliviera, the proprietors of this downtown Edmonton restaurant. Sabor has been renamed and rebranded, their third restaurant Urbano Pizza Co. has opened next door, and Sabor has become 100% Ocean Wise approved. That's a big list of accomplishments for one year, but the Ocean Wise certification is one of the most exciting for their annual seafood festival. I had the pleasure of attending the kick off to this year's Seafood Festival to preview some of Chef Lino's new dishes. The night started off with a bang with the Sabor Caesar Shot: a Malpeque oyster topped with sturgeon caviar and served with a Caesar shot featuring Eau Claire Three Point Vodka. I love that Sabor chose to feature Eau Claire Distillery - as Alberta's first craft distillery, their spirits are sure to impress if you haven't tried them yet! Each table was offered a Pinchos Board, featuring some of the items available on the menu at Bodega Tapas & Wine, to kick off the evening. Pinchos, which are related to tapas, differ such that pinchos are often presented spiked with toothpicks. In Spanish culture, the toothpicks serve as a method of picking up your food, but also as a way to charge you for how much you've eaten. Luckily Sabor doesn't charge based on toothpick count, because I would have had to shell out a lot of money! Our board for the evening featured Sabor's Aceitonas (house marinated olives, $5), octopus and mussel salad ($6, pictured above), crab fritters, seared scallops on pork belly, and snails in red wine with chorizo. The scallops and pork belly were a hit at our table, with the crispy crab fritters a close second. Olives, octopus and snail are such polarizing dishes to begin with, so I found that at our table there was not much in-between, you either liked the dish or you didn't. Our second starter for the evening was Chef Lino's play on Fish and Chips, featuring deep fried lake smelt and piri piri spiced chips. The fish were battered and fried to have a crisp coating, and the piri piri chips had a light seasoning to them. Fair warning though, the lake smelt are deep fried whole, so you chew on the small, edible bones with each bite. Unfortunately the fish and chips are not on the Seafood Festival menu, but Chef Lino will be featuring them once in a while throughout August. Next up was the beautiful Crudo Con Pebre ($24), featuring fresh Red Spring Salmon, Ahi Tuna, BC Coast Halibut, and BC Scallops. The raw seafood was topped with a simple combination of diced tomato, onion, garlic, cilantro, olive oil, and lemon which allowed the natural sweetness of each component to shine through. If you're a sashimi fan, this dish is for you. The following course was a Sardine Flatbread, paying tribute to Urbano Pizza Co. next door. The flatbread was light and covered in a briny onion and anchovy spread that I could not stop eating. Combined with the black olives and portions of sardines, I quite enjoyed this course for the evening. Entrees that evening kicked off with Grilled Humboldt Squid & Prawns ($18) on a bed of chorizo and white bean puree. This squid, otherwise known as the Red Devil, was cooked until soft and very easy to chew. I personally prefer my squid with more bite and chew (like most Asians!), so this dish may not be for everyone. What I really did enjoy though was the bean puree - rich, creamy, and with a kick of heat from the chorizo! Despite having tried a wide variety of tasty seafood dishes, the star of the evening for me was the Bacon Wrapped Sturgeon on Puttanesca Sauce ($32). Sturgeon flesh is quite under-appreciated given that the prized caviar is what most people are after. It was great to see this fish as the star of the plate, and the firmer texture made for a substantial protein.There was smokiness from the bacon, salt and acidity from the sauce, and natural sweetness from the fish to bring everything together. To finish off our family style meal everyone was treated to Mama Margarita's Pudim Flan. This flan is one of Chef Lino's favourite desserts made by his mother, and she finally caved and gave him the recipe. This Portuguese custard is creamy and sweet, and you can taste the richness of the eggs. Word on the street is that this custard is soon to become a gelato flavour at Urbano! While Sabor serves up seafood on their menu throughout the year, the best time to enjoy all that the restaurant has to offer is during the seafood festival. If you can't decide on a specific dish, Chef Lino is also offering off menu family-style dining at $55/person. It's great value and fun for the whole table! The seafood is fresh, the dishes are inventive, and best of all, everything is 100% Ocean Wise. What's stopping you?

text: The approach that I'm going to take with rating the telecom/internet/cable industry is going to be from the ground up. As an industry, they just seem to not really like their customers. All of these companies start at one star and work their way up from there. From the beginning of the business relationship, you are typically given the bait-and-switch - you know, you get your 1 year intro rate, then prices begin to rise significantly. Since that is the standard, a person shopping for internet/phone/cable service then knows that they need to find two prices to do comparison shopping: the intro rate, and the standard rate. The intro rate is easy to find, but you need to be Sherlock Holmes sometimes to find the standard rate - it's exhausting and annoying! Then, to get answers you typically have to go through a call center - yay! Some of these call centers are overseas, and some are in the US. Either way, they are time consuming to have to deal with. Okay, now you're signed into a contract with one of these companies. Well, the service usually rolls without a hitch, but let me relate an experience that I had with Clearwire/Sprint: the service was getting bad and I was experiencing outages. When I'd call for support, they'd hand me to online tech support that seems to work off a queue card and the typical problem that they'd lead you on to would be that if you were using your own router then according to them the problem was the third party router - this was the problem every time! I'd eventually have to suggest that they needed to reset my connection on their switch to resolve the issue - fixed the problem every time. One time the problem was bad and was not getting resolved no matter what they did. We kept going back and forth for a few weeks until my problem was finally escalated to someone that could check the coverage area - it turns out that Sprint/Clearwire was pulling out of my market area and failed to tell me! These companies are so annoying to deal with and not one of them seems to want to break the mold. So here we go for this company... Just dropping this on Clearwire/Sprint (whoever owns it now), since they are the initial source of my disgust with the ISP industry.
label: NEG

In other places I have been, the manager or owner comes around after dinner to ask how me the meal was and thank you for your business. This did not happen here. Our waiter barely even came back to our table after our main coarse was finished. Anyway, I think we'll just stick to what we know is good next time and return to our regular Mr. John's Steakhouse.

My "Serve me indicator" (or whatever the Brazilian restaurant industry calls it) was green up each time he passed my table and I tried to make eye contact with him just for grins. He totally snubbed me. I'm telling you, this guy was something else. If you watched him as he wandered around the restaurant you would see him walk normal if he thought no one could see him from the dining room. As soon as he stepped into the dining room he would start limping like he just broke his leg. Crazy stuff. Maybe he was telling the young girls he was flirting with that it was a war injury. Who knows? Just for the record, the girls were not flirting back with this loser. I felt sorry for them for having to deal with this guy. I've traveled worldwide for 29 years for business and pleasure, so I'm qualified to judge the service of a restaurant from a diner's point of view. I continue to be amazed that a restaurant will put people like him in a position to interact with patrons. What purpose does it serve? I guess it will remain a mystery to me. I wonder if the owner of this restaurant actually reads reviews of their restaurant on high profile websites like this. I travel on an expense account, so the only skin I have in this interaction is my time and my digestive health. For the good people that travel to Nashville TN and spend their hard earned money for a good dining experience, please be aware that Rodizio's is not all that it should be based on my personal experience. text: This must be my favorite place on the wank. Leaving this store fills my kitchen for weeks with the satisfaction that the cost was less than your average meal for 4 at Chilis. The vegetable and produce section is not only eccentric, but quality. Bok choy galore, and odd mushrooms to test. The regular items from other common good stores are still available, and usually cheaper. Do you like fresh fish? King fish, red snapper, grouper, squid and on and on are available daily, wild caught from the gulf. Shrimps of all sizes and sea depths. Salted preserved cod is awesome to experiment with. All the bean curd paste and kimchi you can ever use, and other soy products essential for Miso soups are affordable, organized, and readily available. Ramen. Ramen. And more ramen. I usually walk out with 20 packets of these crazy dehydrated suckers. Buy packed seaweed, dehydrated fungus and jellyfish, and black bean paste in one isle! Go to the next and find the sweetest candy ever. Eat lots of rice? Buy it by the burlap sack. Don't have pots or plates? They have high quality selections. Want to steam some dumplings you bought here? Get a cheap bamboo steamer before you leave. Don't forget to pick up and fresh bahn mi at the far end. Also check out the other baked goods, frozen proteins and dim sum. Really kind service from the check out folks. When leaving, you can also buy beautiful bamboo shoot, and even DVDs. It's crazy the collection of items they have. And everything is great. Ok, so while it isn't a glitzy place, not recently renovated, who really cares? Cutting on the glamour makes for more better prices. What's really cool is you can spend a whole day here, getting a haircut, massage, getting tax work done, enjoying coffee, and even sitting at restaurant. Lastly, what's most surprising is that there are tons of locals who shop here as their primary supermarket. It really is that resourceful. Save money, eat better.

Happy Hour is from 3 to 6 and it features one wine and one entree. Note: If you check in on Yelp, it unlocks a coupon. We chose the happy hour wine and it was poured nearly to the brim (small glass, but still a nice pour). The app we chose was the hummus platter that features three different varieties as well as rice crackers. It was delicious and seriously filled us both. With the two happy hour wines, one appetizer, and the check-in coupon, our bill was seriously just over $10. An excellent way to spend the evening. After a number of $4-8 drinks, I slammed a late night burger from Burger Bros. I had a great night sleep in the King bed and checked out the next morning. For the room (with taxes), dinner and drinks, I spent about $220. The key is finding people who want to have fun gambling and play with them. Maybe I should have taken a shower earlier than 10:30am though. - One of the dealers didn't move very fast and was kind of boring. Might be better to move those dealers to weekday AM shifts. I will definitely be coming back for a girls night out! Tips: Lazia is open for lunch and also has a takeout menu. There are $4 drink specials on ladies night and most importantly- there is free customer parking!! Access to customer parking: Enter the Edmonton City Center parkade from 103 Street which is across from the Grand Hotel. Pull a ticket and you will need to turn right and go down to the lower levels. Look for the Bay Parkade which is two levels in the basement below. There are blue Bay Parkade signs on the ceiling to direct you towards a triple garage door on your left side. Drive close to it and it will open up for you to enter. Proceed to the ticket station and insert the ticket you have into the slot to raise the bar and proceed to the lower parkade. Work your way towards the left where the sliding glass doors are and park in a public spot and leave the ticket on the dash board of your car. Use the elevator to go up to the main floor where we are across the Bay. Upon exiting pay with a voucher that you will be at the restaurant.

text: 5 of us including 2 kids arrived about 6:00 on a Saturday. The main parking lot was already full but plenty of parking on other side. However, some of those must have been employee's cars as there weren't quite that many diners inside. The decor is welcoming, very nice, looks and feels Thai. 5 stars for Thai ambiance. We were seated right away and several other groups came in as we looked over the menus. We had printed out some coupons from their website but forgot them at home. I pulled up the coupon on my phone and before we ordered anything we explained we had forgot the hard copies. The waitress said we could not use that, they had to be printed out. It's 2015, imo, showing your phone should be acceptable now. Also, NO kids menu which is very disappointing so plan on spending adult prices for your kids meals. 5 Thai teas, Crab Rangoon and Spring Rolls to start. Thai tea is so good and addicting as it should be. Rangoon was made with curry powder which I hadn't had before, it was different, and good. The (2) Spring Rolls were standard fare. Being our first visit there, and one of our groups 1st Thai experience ever, we both ordered Pad Thai. I know it's Thai version 1.0 but I like it. Their Pad Thai comes with 2 shrimp and chicken. It was quite good. I would say that the sauce however did not have quite as much flavor as others I've had. I've seen this before with Pad Thai, it seems the lighter the color, the less flavor. It's not a spice/heat issue either so maybe it's the ratio of fish sauce or tamarind? It was still good and I would get it again. My newbie decided to kick it up a notch with the spice tray and she liked it. The wife got the Amazing, a peanut sauce dish which was quite different than the "Amazing" she gets at our usual Thai place. Not what she expected, she really liked it and would get it again. It was quite spicy though which was not indicated as such on the menu. One of the kids ordered their usual sushi rolls which they said were really good, but not quite as good as they had at Jimmy's last week. The other ordered the Broccoli entree with Chicken. That dish was made with Royal Oyster sauce and we asked for it on the side, we also asked to substitute baby corn for carrots, all of which came out as requested. The broccoli was cooked perfectly with good flavor, and the kid even dipped the chicken in the oyster sauce which was also very good. I would totally order that dish for myself next time. Being a party of 5 they automatically add 18% gratuity to the check which totaled $106. That may sound expensive but we didnt order any expensive dishes. It adds up though, Thai teas are $3.00 each, we ordered 2 appetizers, and 2 sushi rolls, and one kid who we can normally feed for $5-6 had to order an $11 adult meal. Overall the atmosphere, food and portions were very good, the service was decent, and it was a nice dining experience. We will go back. 4 stars is my highest rating for a restaurant like this as I reserve my 5th star for rare incredible experiences and/or very high end establishments.

text: I was so disappointed with the service at this restaurant today. It was obvious that the place was busy, but as out-of-towners I could only assume that this was the norm and that the knew what they were doing. Obviously, that was not the case. With two small children in tow, we waited over an hour and a half from the time we walked into the place, an hour of that being time between ordering and receiving our food. No one kept us updated on timing, notified us of any delays at all, or checked in. When my husband finally flagged someone down to ask about the delay, our server gave no apology and instead said, "other people got here first." WHAT?! Obviously they were busy, but it would have been simple at that point to say, "wow, sorry about that, we're totally understaffed today." Instead the response was downright rude. I was so annoyed (and hangry!) that I straight out told our server that if she would just apologize for the 1 hour delay on food, it wouldn't be as big a deal, which she did grudgingly. As we left the restaurant, I stopped to speak to the manager. I explained in less than 2 minutes of talk time (as opposed to a "twenty minute rant" as the business owner's yelp response claimed) that we had a really bad experience, that we waited for over an hour, that our kids were hungry, and that their wait staff was unapologetic. At NO POINT during that talk did I say that anyone was awful, make any personal attacks, or exaggerations. I simply stated what had happened, said that an apology would have fixed it, and explained that I was saying this so that they would have the opportunity to fix this problem for other guests in the future. The manager I spoke with was understanding and apologetic, and seemed reasonable about it all. I thought we might have just had a fluke of a bad experience, but the fact that the business owner went on yelp to accuse me on my husband Bill K's post that I was "ranting in front of my child" is rude, unnecessary, and factually incorrect. Telling people in a straightforward way about a problem and how they could fix it, without personal attacks, is not a "rant," nor is it something that should be hidden from children (my personal argument is that it's good to teach kids to advocate for themselves within reason, but that's my own personal view). And, side note, "never seen a rant like this before"???!! You have led a truly charmed life as a restaurant owner. Congratulations, owner/yelper of The Mex Authentic - not only did you ruin my lunch, now you've ruined my day by calling me out personally as some kind of crazy lady and inspiring me to write a bad review (which, as is obvious in my yelp profile, I rarely do!). What poor management of a business, when it would have been so easy to just say "we're sorry" and move on. UPDATE: In response to the owner's comment below, I just want to clarify that an apology sounds like this, "I'm sorry." It doesn't sound like a passive-aggressive list of personal attacks and excuses, followed by "I wish you well." Furthermore, there was absolutely no apology for the personal attack in your response to my husband's post claiming that I went on a "twenty minute rant against your manager without giving him time to get a word in." Wishing me well doesn't change that that was a histrionic exaggeration that deserves an apology in and of itself. I am not a difficult customer - I made no special requests, I communicated my valid feelings and experiences without exaggeration or personal attacks, and yet you have represented your business by going on the web to do both. I guess all I have to say is . . . I wish you well.

This was, of course after having my emails ignored by the program chair, the dean of my program, and the instructor himself, as well as being told by the director of the school that I should be glad I didn't get an 'F' as a final grade. This school is also chock FULL of people of questionable character. Many of the students LOOK like they're on drugs much of the time, some of them SMELL of drugs, and several will ADMIT to being high in class every week. Not only that, but the level of morality that people here have is often very low. For instance, several students have had their laptops stolen, when their backs were turned, right out of their bags or off the table. Then, you have the issue with having to go in and have your schedule corrected each quarter, when you're not a full-time student, yet they sign you up as one each new quarter, but state that the system only shows you part-time, and should only schedule you as such. Lets also not forget about the BLATANT, and FLAT-OUT lies they will tell you to hook you into attending. I was told by my recruiter that credits transfer very easily, that you can test out of up to 50% of the classes in the NSA program, and that, if necessary, the school understands when you need to miss class for a week or so, due to life's events. All of these were false informations! ITT is only nationally accredited, which means that any other school, such as IUPUI, which is both nationally and locally credited, will not accept your credits. It turns out that there are very few school that will, period. You cannot test out of up to 50% of the classes in the NSA program, because you cannot test out of their made-up classes, like "Stategies for the Technical Professional," which is a course on MS Office, and you can't test out of core classes. You CAN test out of General Educations courses, like Math and Composition, but there are only a few of these in the program. The test out program is very rigged as well, so as to keep you from testing out when you've missed the small test out window. Credits WILL transfer in pretty easily, although sometimes you have to fight them to accept them. The school is also NOT very forgiving when missing class. First of all, if you don't inform the instructor that you're missing class, the school will call you to ask why you weren't there, because attendance is taken for each class. Also, most classes have "Lab Time," whether the class really has any labs or not, and your grade for those is often only given by showing up for class, with no way to make it up for missing. Some instructors will just simply not allow you to make up work, either, regardless of why you missed or whether you planned it with them ahead of time. So, often, if you miss a class, you're receiving zeros in the grade book, which most of the time can't be redeemed. One of the most dubious things they've done in the past couple years is to inject an extra course into the curriculum, after we had already signed up, and are most of the way through our degree program. We now must take "Advanced Strategies for the Technical Professional," which includes most of the topics covered in other classes. So, this class is actually just a redundancy, which we all (we students) feel is a money ploy, since we will have to pay for that class. The information from an instructor is that this extra class was included so that military students, who have their tuition paid for by the government, can be considered at least 3/4-time for the duration of their degree, as the government does not pay when they don't got at least 3/4-time. The way it originally worked out is that the last quarter of the degree would only be one class a week, which is only 4.5 credit hours, and drops the government assistance for that quarter. So, it really is just a way for the school to rake in the money. In all, I implore you to FIND A BETTER SCHOOL TO GIVE YOUR MONEY TO!!!
